issues.section: Lab 9: two independent samples, then a campaign (production.sh)
issues.quote: grep -q '^/musr/run/randomOption 1' 201_prod.mac || echo '/musr/run/randomOption 1' | cat - 201_prod.mac > tmp && mv tmp 201_prod.mac
issues.problem: && and || have equal precedence, so this is (grep || pipeline) && mv. In the normal case (sed already wrote randomOption 1) grep succeeds, tmp is never written, mv fails, and with set -e the script exits before the job loop. Verified in bash: 'mv: cannot stat tmp', exit 1.
issues.fix: if ! grep -q '^/musr/run/randomOption 1' 201_prod.mac; then { echo '/musr/run/randomOption 1'; cat 201_prod.mac; } > tmp && mv tmp 201_prod.mac; fi

issues.quote: Below about 10 µm in plastic, lowering the cut no longer changes the e⁻ threshold. Why? ... (b) Geant4 never produces secondaries below its 990 eV lower limit
issues.problem: code/week06/cut_thresholds_g4_11.4.json gives plastic e- thresholds of 14.5 keV at 0.01 mm, 1.74 keV at 0.003 mm and 0.99 keV only at 0.001 mm; the 10 um statement is true for gammas, not electrons. 990 eV is the default low edge of the production-threshold table (changeable with /cuts/setLowEdge), and de-excitation can still produce lower-energy secondaries.
issues.fix: 'Below about 1 µm ... e⁻ threshold' (or ask about gammas at 30 µm); answer: 'the production-threshold table starts at 990 eV by default (/cuts/setLowEdge)'.

issues.section: Check the integrator before blaming the physics
issues.quote: The 1 GeV σ differs from step 3 (0.0031 against 0.0040) because the run produces different random scattering, not because of integration: compare in units of its own error.
issues.problem: reconstruct.py quotes np.std, which on 1000 events is tail-dominated; the lab itself promises '±3% relative on σ'. On your own CSV files I get std 0.0040 but central-68% half-width 0.0029 at 1 GeV, driven by 5 events beyond 5 widths. The text teaches the wrong estimator for the week's headline number and explains a 25% jump as statistics. The toy uses the 68% half-width, so toy and lab disagree in definition.
issues.fix: Report the central-68% half-width (or a Gaussian core fit) in reconstruct.py, and say tails are scattering/delta-ray outliers.

issues.quote: More muons would show whether the 1.4σ is statistics or a small bias, for example the few nanoseconds each muon spends in flight before it stops.
issues.problem: A constant time offset shifts the phase φ, not the fitted frequency f; it cannot bias the slope.
issues.fix: Give a mechanism that does change f (field non-uniformity seen by the stopping distribution, binning/fit-start effects, or the MT decay-channel race) or drop the example.

issues.section: Course-W12-b (also referenced in week10 · Recover the field)
issues.quote: G4DecayWithSpin writes the muon spin into G4VDecayChannel::parent_polarization, a plain member of a decay table that all threads share ... no physics effect visible at this precision, but bit-level reproducibility is gone.
issues.problem: I checked G4DecayWithSpin.cc (lines ~98 and ~174): the diagnosis is right and is a real finding. But a race on the polarization means a positron can occasionally be generated with another thread's muon spin - a correctness bug that dilutes A0, not only a reproducibility issue. The Week 10 app still defaults to SetNumberOfThreads(2).
issues.fix: File a Geant4 bug report and cite it; describe it as a data race affecting physics; run the uSR reference app single-threaded by default (or make the channel polarization thread-local in a patched local copy).

issues.section: 5.1 Deposited is not detected (Code microscope · MuonSD.cc)
issues.quote: hit->AddEvis(edep / (1. + kBirks * edep / length));   // Birks per step
issues.problem: Fine as pedagogy, but modern Geant4 already provides Birks via G4EmSaturation (material->GetIonisation()->SetBirksConstant(); G4LossTableManager::Instance()->EmSaturation()->VisibleEnergyDepositionAtAStep(step)), which handles secondaries/particle type properly. Experts will ask why it is not mentioned.
issues.fix: Add a 'In production code' note showing the G4EmSaturation call.

issues.section: Scan the production cut / Run B: the EM-only list (expected output)
issues.quote: secondaries per event, by particle:   e- 2.387   gamma 1.358 / by creator :  muIoni 6.649 ...
issues.problem: RunAction.cc prints one species per line and a 'CPU time per event' line; 'by creator :' is not a label the code prints. With grep -A4 the student sees the CPU line and only e-. Output is labelled 'expected' but is a hand-condensed version.
issues.fix: Paste verbatim output (or label it 'condensed').

issues.quote: if (edep <= 0.) return false; ... if (it == fTime.end() || t < it->second) fTime[id] = t;  /  'Using the counter time instead of the truth decay time changes f by less than its error'
issues.problem: CounterSD has no energy threshold, so any deposit 'fires' a counter - exactly what Week 5 forbids. I ran the week10 app (60k muons, 11.4 harness): 0.3% (U) and 0.8% (D) of counter 'hits' have det_time_start about 0.8 ns, i.e. microseconds BEFORE the decay, with median deposit 30 keV (delta rays/soft particles from the incoming muon); 5% of the other hits deposit < 0.1 MeV. In --measured mode these early times put events at t=0, which is why f moves by ~0.85 sigma on the same events (my run: 1.3579 -> 1.3549, 0.6 sigma). They also enter hitU/hitD in truth mode as 'positrons'.
issues.fix: Apply an event-level threshold per counter (e.g. 0.3-0.5 MeV) and take the time of the first deposit above threshold (or of the first e+ step); then show that truth and measured f agree to << sigma. Mention it in the text as a Week 5 callback.
